description:
## Context
The Engine B metric backend parses per-file entries from scc JSON, but `_metric_invoke` invokes `scc --format json <repo>` without `--by-file`. With maintained scc 3.7.0, the language summary includes `Files: []` unless `--by-file` is requested. Therefore a present scc process can run successfully while `rebar.builtin.smell.metric-oversize` sees no files and can never emit its documented over-800-LOC matches.

The analogous code-health adapter defect was fixed by closed bug rapid-cuboid-velvetcrab, whose history explicitly notes grounding `_scc_files` is a separate consumer. Current coverage-reconstruction tests use a 50-LOC fixture or force tool absence, so they do not exercise the positive metric threshold path.

## Reproduction
- Run `scc --format json tests/unit/grounding` and inspect each language `Files` array: it is empty.
- Compare with `scc --by-file --format json tests/unit/grounding`: per-file entries are present.
- Inspect `src/rebar/grounding/engine_b_backends.py::_metric_invoke`: its command omits `--by-file` while `_scc_files` depends on `Files`.

## Plan
- Use rebar-debug to reproduce with a real scc binary and an over-800-code-line fixture, then prove the exact argv cause before editing.
- Add a physically withheld RED oracle that observes a real or argv-faithful scc boundary and fails when `--by-file` is absent.
- Correct the grounding metric invocation without changing thresholds or fail-open semantics.
- Add positive match, below-threshold no-match, invalid-output, nonzero-exit, and tool-absent coverage.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A present scc run over a file above the configured LOC threshold emits a normalized metric match for that file.
- [ ] A present scc run below the threshold emits no fabricated match.
- [ ] The scc command requests per-file JSON explicitly; checked by an argv-sensitive test.
- [ ] Tool absence, timeout/nonzero failure, and invalid JSON remain fail-open evidence outcomes.
- [ ] The focused grounding backend tests pass with the held-out exact-defect oracle.

## Verification
- Run the focused grounding metric tests with the worktree virtualenv.
- Run the repository lint and typecheck gates.
- Run the default test suite before landing through Gerrit.

file_impact.reason: correct scc argv to request per-file JSON
add metric present-path and argv-sensitive regression coverage

error); `test_applier_reschedule.py::test_exit_reschedule_constant_is_distinct` (`==75`);

`_FIELD_WEIGHTS` values); `test_code_review_artifact.py::test_code_review_excluded_from_
jira_sync` (asserts `code_review` present/absent in reconciler source). VALIDATED.

## What

assert EXIT_RESCHEDULE via the reschedule path that returns it; prove the fs_tools cluster
via the existing identity/reuse seam; exercise ranking that `_FIELD_WEIGHTS` drives; run

description:
## Context / Problem
`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_wiki_render_hardening.py::test_rendered_output_is_byte_identical_to_the_landed_renderer` intermittently kills its pytest-xdist worker on the macOS py3.13 `Verified` cell, reddening the whole matrix job and costing changes a `Verified -1` they did not earn (observed on change 1731 ps2; the identical commit passed in change 1734).

## Root cause — CONFIRMED, reproduced deterministically
Two measurements, both in this worktree, name the mechanism:

1. **The crash is a per-test-timeout kill, not OOM and not a pandoc fault.** CI runs the unit suite with `--timeout=300 --timeout-method=thread` (`.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml`). pytest-timeout's *thread* method calls `os._exit(1)` from its timer thread, so the xdist worker process dies outright — no traceback, no assertion text. Reproduced by lowering only the budget: `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_wiki_render_hardening.py -n 2 --dist worksteal --timeout=20 --timeout-method=thread` emits `[gw0] node down: Not properly terminated` followed by `worker 'gw0' crashed while running '...::test_rendered_output_is_byte_identical_to_the_landed_renderer'` — byte-identical in shape to the CI report.
2. **The test's cost is unbounded and load-dependent.** It walks the whole committed corpus in ONE test function: 884 renderable units, each rendered twice (`_convert` plus the `_legacy_convert` oracle) = ~1768 serial pandoc spawns. Measured **91.6s** idle; under saturating CPU pressure (2x `hw.ncpu` spinners, the `fade-ea90` precedent) the same test measured **504.8s** — 1.7x past the 300s guard. macOS is the scarcest cell in the runner pool, so that contention is routine, which is why only that cell reds.

The osprey cross-worker sharing commit `48a3ba0b8a` does **not** cover this file — it touched `test_wiki_render_corpus.py` only, and its `corpus_pass1` artifact holds pass-1 renders of whole bodies, not the per-unit `_convert`/oracle pairs this test compares. Siblings measured healthy post-48a3ba0b8a (worst call 12.5s), so this test is the last one of the shape.

## Approach
Make the per-test cost **bounded and independent of both load and corpus size**, without touching what is compared. Replace the single monolithic loop in `test_rendered_output_is_byte_identical_to_the_landed_renderer` with a **chunk-parametrized** test: `_renderable_units()` is computed once at module import, sliced into fixed-size batches by a new module constant `_EQUIVALENCE_CHUNK = 40`, and the test takes the chunk as a `pytest.mark.parametrize` argument keyed by chunk index.

Why this shape and not the alternatives:
- **Fixed chunk size is the class fix.** Growing the corpus adds *cases*, never lengthens a case, so the per-test budget can never be re-crossed by fixture growth — the failure mode is closed structurally, not tuned away.
- Every one of the 884 units is still compared against the oracle with real pandoc; `_EQUIVALENCE_STRIDE` stays 1. The byte-identity property the test exists to protect is untouched.
- 23 cases at ~4.2s idle each leaves ~13x headroom even at the 5.5x inflation measured above, and xdist can now spread the work across workers instead of pinning it to one.
- Explicitly NOT doing: raising `--timeout`, adding a rerun/flaky marker, or asserting on elapsed time (the wall-clock-assert gate forbids the last).

A failing comparison currently reports only `assert <str> == <str>` from an anonymous loop iteration. The chunked assertion carries the unit's **global corpus index** in its message, so a future failure names which unit moved.

To keep chunking from silently dropping units, add `test_the_equivalence_chunks_cover_every_renderable_unit`: a pandoc-free test asserting the concatenation of all chunks equals `_renderable_units()` and that the total is >= 100 (the evidence floor the old inline `assert len(sampled) >= 100` provided, which moves out of the per-chunk body since no single chunk meets it).

The module docstring gains a short cost-discipline note mirroring the one `test_wiki_render_corpus.py` already carries, so the next author sees why the parametrization exists.

## Scope
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_wiki_render_hardening.py` — chunk-parametrize the equivalence test, add the coverage guard, document the cost discipline. This is the only file changed; the renderer itself (`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_family/wiki_render.py`) is deliberately untouched, since the fault is in the test's cost profile, not in `_convert`.

## Testing
Test-only change, so the tests ARE the deliverable; verification is by measurement:
- Happy path: the full file passes with real pandoc and every unit still compared — `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_wiki_render_hardening.py -q --durations=0`, with no call above ~10s idle.
- Load path (the reproduction, re-run after the fix): the same file under 2x `hw.ncpu` CPU spinners must complete with every individual call well inside 300s, where the pre-fix test measured 504.8s.
- Failure path: the new coverage guard fails if a chunk is dropped — verified by temporarily truncating the chunk list in a scratch run and observing the guard red before reverting.
- Regression path: the whole suite under CI's exact invocation, `pytest -m "not integration and not external" -n 3 --dist worksteal --timeout=300 --timeout-method=thread`, must show no worker crash.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The mechanism is recorded on this ticket with its deterministic reproduction — verified by the presence of the lowered-timeout command and the 91.6s/504.8s pair above, both re-runnable in this worktree.
- [ ] No single test in `test_wiki_render_hardening.py` exceeds ~10s idle — verified by `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_wiki_render_hardening.py --durations=0` showing every `call` under that bound.
- [ ] Per-test cost is bounded by construction, not by tuning — verified by reading `_EQUIVALENCE_CHUNK`: chunk size is a fixed constant, so corpus growth adds cases rather than extending any case.
- [ ] The byte-identity property is not weakened — verified by `test_the_equivalence_chunks_cover_every_renderable_unit` asserting the chunks reassemble to exactly `_renderable_units()` (884 units, >= 100), with `_EQUIVALENCE_STRIDE` still 1 and real pandoc on both sides.
- [ ] The fix is not a timeout raise or a retry marker — verified by the diff touching no workflow file and adding no rerun marker or elapsed-time assertion.
- [ ] A `Verified +1` run on the change passes the macOS py3.13 cell.

file_impact.reason: chunk-parametrize the corpus equivalence test so per-test cost is bounded and load-independent; add a chunk-coverage guard

description:
# The DC store-copy fixture hard-fails on `git fetch origin tickets` and swallows git's reason

## Context / Problem

Live External Integration run **31587452003** (2026-08-12, head `b13173bb7d`) ended the DC
harness at `1 failed, 59 passed, 1 xfailed, 1 error in 2471.11s`. The **error** is a fixture
failure, not a cell defect:

    ERROR tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_dc_mutations.py::test_outbound_unassign_round_trips
      - subprocess.CalledProcessError: Command '['git','fetch','origin','tickets']'
        returned non-zero exit status 128.

It aborts at setup of `dc_store_copy_repo` (`tests/external/live_jira_dc/_dc_fixtures.py`,
lines 139-141 at origin/main `cc69cc1179`), which fetches the live `tickets` branch in the
outer CI checkout and then `git archive FETCH_HEAD | tar -x` to seed a scrubbed store copy.

**Two problems, and the second is why the first is still unexplained:**

1. **The failure is undiagnosable, by construction.** The call is
   `subprocess.run(..., capture_output=True, check=True)`: `capture_output=True` routes git's
   stderr into a captured buffer, and `check=True` then raises `CalledProcessError` whose
   string form carries only the exit status. Git's own message — the one line that would say
   whether this was auth, a missing ref, a refspec miss under the CI partial clone, or a
   network error — is discarded. From the run log, exit 128 is all there is. The `git archive`
   (142-144) and `git ls-tree` (151-156) calls beside it have the identical shape.
2. **The fetch is a single un-retried network call** on the critical path of a 41-minute live
   job, so any transient blip takes the cell out as an ERROR.

## Approach

Fix the diagnostic FIRST — it is what makes the retry policy decidable.

* Add a module-level `_run_git(argv, cwd, ...)` helper in `_dc_fixtures.py` that runs the
  command with captured output and, on a non-zero exit, raises `RuntimeError` carrying the
  joined argv (which names the remote and branch), the exit status, and git's captured
  **stderr** verbatim. Route the fetch, archive and ls-tree calls through it.
* Then add bounded retry to the fetch only: `_fetch_tickets(...)` retries a failing fetch a
  fixed small number of times with a backoff sleep (injectable for test), and on final failure
  re-raises the diagnostic error. Policy is **retry-then-fail**, not retry-then-skip, so a
  genuine misconfiguration still reds the lane rather than silently dropping coverage.

The helpers are plain module-level functions, so the unit tier can load `_dc_fixtures.py` by
path (`importlib.util.spec_from_file_location`, the pattern already used by
`tests/unit/test_live_dc_isolation_controls_59b2.py`) and drive them with a stubbed
`subprocess.run` — no harness image, no live lane, verified on every commit.

## Scope

* `tests/external/live_jira_dc/_dc_fixtures.py` — new `_run_git` / `_fetch_tickets` helpers;
  the `dc_store_copy_repo` fetch/archive/ls-tree calls routed through them.
* `tests/unit/test_dc_store_copy_fetch_diagnostics.py` — new unit cell (repo tier).

## Testing

All acceptance evidence is repo-tier and runs under plain `pytest tests/unit/...`; the live
lane is operator-spend and is NOT a gate for this ticket (see "Follow-up", below).

* stubbed `subprocess.run` returning exit 128 with a distinctive stderr line proves the raised
  message carries that stderr, the remote, the branch and the status — and the negative
  control proves it goes RED against the old `check=True` shape (a `CalledProcessError` whose
  text does not contain the stderr).
* stubbed `subprocess.run` failing once then succeeding proves the fetch retries and returns.
* stubbed `subprocess.run` always failing proves the attempt count is bounded and the final
  raise still carries git's stderr.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `_dc_fixtures.py`'s git fetch failure path raises an error whose message contains git's
      captured stderr verbatim plus the remote, the branch and the exit status — proven by a
      unit cell with a stubbed failing `subprocess.run`
- [ ] the same holds for the `git archive` and `git ls-tree` calls in `dc_store_copy_repo`
      (no `capture_output=True` + `check=True` pair is left in that fixture)
- [ ] the fetch retries a transient failure a bounded number of times before failing — proven
      by one stub that fails once then succeeds and one that always fails, the latter
      asserting the attempt count is capped and the final error still names git's stderr
- [ ] no cell is deleted, skipped or `xfail`ed; `make lint`, `make typecheck` and
      `pytest tests/unit/test_dc_store_copy_fetch_diagnostics.py` pass

## Follow-up (deliberately NOT an AC here)

Confirming on a live run that `test_outbound_unassign_round_trips` either passes or now fails
with git's actual reason requires a Live External Integration run, which is operator-spend and
cannot be triggered from this ticket. The next scheduled live run reads the improved message;
if it still errors, the log will finally name the cause and that becomes its own ticket.

## Not in scope

The other residual in the same run —
`test_dc_mutations.py::test_outbound_create_stamps_both_provenance_markers` failing with
`rebar create failed (exit 1): Error: git commit failed while holding lock: git timed out
after 30s` — is the tracker write-lock contention family and is already tracked by
`royal-weariless-zebrafish` (`10c3-5a33-2e25-4584`). Do not fold it in here.

file_impact.reason: add _run_git/_fetch_tickets helpers that surface git stderr and retry the tickets fetch; route fetch/archive/ls-tree through them
new repo-tier cell driving the helpers with a stubbed subprocess.run

description:
# `rebar comment <id> --body-file <path>` stores the literal string \`--body-file\` and exits 0

## Observed twice, by two different sessions

`rebar comment` takes its body POSITIONALLY (`Usage: rebar comment <ticket_id> <body>`). It has no
`--body`/`--body-file` option. When invoked with one anyway, the flag token is accepted AS the body:
the stored comment is the 11-byte string \`--body-file\` (or the 6-byte \`--body\`), the intended
content is silently discarded, and **the command exits 0** so nothing signals the loss.

Evidence in the live store right now:
- ticket b690 comments 5-9: five stubs of length 11, 11, 11, 11, 6 — an entire session's root-cause
  analysis, fix rationale, blast-radius audit and live evidence, all lost.
- session log 55a9 comment 5: also \`--body-file\`, written by an EARLIER session. So this is not a
  one-off slip; the same footgun has now cost two independent sessions their durable record.

## Why this is worse than a normal CLI usage error

rebar's own guidance (AGENTS.md) is emphatic that the ticket store — not scratch notes — is the
durable, shared trail, and that agents should write progress and findings back as comments. This
failure mode silently defeats exactly that instruction, and it does so in the least detectable way:
- exit code 0
- no stderr
- a comment DOES appear, so a \`len(comments)\` check (which is the natural way to confirm "did my
  write land?") passes while the content is gone
- the loss is only discovered later by something that READS the content — in this case the completion
  verifier, which correctly failed a ticket for having "no concrete attestation recorded" because the
  attestation genuinely was not there.

The cost is not the retyping. It is that work believed to be recorded is not, and downstream gates
make correct-but-confusing decisions on the missing evidence.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] a body argument that begins with \`-\` is REJECTED with a non-zero exit and a message naming the
      correct form, rather than stored — unless the user clearly meant it (see below)
- [ ] the escape hatch exists and is documented: a body that legitimately starts with \`-\` can still be
      written (conventionally via \`--\`, e.g. \`rebar comment <id> -- "-starts with a dash"\`)
- [ ] the same guard covers every positional-body command with this shape, not just \`comment\`
      (audit at least \`create\`/\`edit\`/\`session-log\` for the same footgun and fix or document each)
- [ ] a test asserts the REJECTION for \`--body-file <path>\` and \`--body <text>\` specifically, since
      those are the two forms that have actually occurred
- [ ] consider (and decide explicitly, either way) whether to ADD a real \`--body-file\` option: the
      fact that two independent sessions reached for it suggests it is the expected interface for
      long bodies, and shell quoting of multi-KB markdown through a positional arg is awkward
- [ ] no silent truncation or coercion anywhere in the fix: a body that cannot be stored as given must
      fail loudly

## Notes

Filed OUTSIDE epic 061c — unrelated to the LLM provider seam; this is a CLI/store-durability concern.
Found when the completion verifier failed story b690 for missing attestations that had in fact been
written five times over.

## Why
Serial wall-clock is ~N×CI for N ready stacks; batching collapses it to ~1 CI cycle, which is the wall-clock-optimal option under the Free-tier GHA concurrency cap (~3 concurrent runs) where speculation would just queue.
## What
Assemble the queued `Autosubmit` changes/stacks into ONE combined relation chain on current `main`, trigger CI ONCE on the combined tip, and land them together atomically if green (Graphite/bors stack-aware model on Gerrit relation chains).
## Scope
Phase 2. The batching assembly + single-run + atomic land. Verified-casting and batch-failure handling are separate stories. Depends on Phase 1.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Assembles queued changes/stacks into one combined linear chain on the current `main` tip.
- [ ] Triggers exactly ONE CI run on the combined tip (not one per change).
- [ ] On green, submits the whole batch atomically (ancestor-atomic submit); the tested tip == the landed tree.
- [ ] Batch size bounded to one CI run's job budget (fits the GHA concurrency cap); documents the bound.

## Why
Serial wall-clock is ~N×CI for N ready stacks; batching collapses it to ~1 CI cycle, which is the wall-clock-optimal option under the Free-tier GHA concurrency cap where speculation would just queue (the exact concurrent-run count isn't the limiter — `gerrit-verify.yaml` uses a per-change concurrency group).

## What
Assemble the queued `Autosubmit` changes/stacks into ONE combined relation chain on current `main`, and trigger CI ONCE on the combined tip. The batching **algorithm** — combine N non-conflicting changes → one CI pass → atomic land — has precedent in bors/Graphite, **adapted** to Gerrit relation chains (those tools are GitHub-PR-native, not usable on Gerrit).

## Dependencies
Depends on **S2** (`perovskite-frilly-grebe`, 0ee8-08de-bf0f-45ec) — the Phase-1 core loop: batching reuses its selection, rebase, and `is:submittable` machinery, and Phase 2 is a fast-follow on the serial lander.

## Verified-satisfaction (cross-reference, no blocking link)
Per-member `Verified` is satisfied by the single combined-tip run, but **casting** that `Verified +1` per member is owned by **S8** (bot-casts-Verified). This story delivers **assembly + the single CI trigger only**; on green it hands off to S8's cast-Verified + submit. **The handoff is an explicit record** — S7 writes `{member_change_ids[], combined_tip_change_id, tested_sha, run_id}` to the batch state that S8 reads before casting any vote (so S8 binds each vote to a SHA S7 actually assembled + tested). (Prose cross-reference — S7 does not `depends_on` S8, to avoid a cycle.)

## Scope
Phase 2. The batching assembly + single-run trigger. Verified-casting, atomic submit, and batch-failure handling are separate stories (S8, S9).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Assembles queued changes/stacks into one combined linear chain on the current `main` tip, reusing S2's `/rebase:chain` as the building block for cross-stack chain assembly.
- [ ] Triggers exactly ONE CI run on the combined tip (not one per change), dispatching `gerrit-verify.yaml` against the **real combined-tip change's** actual Change-Id / change-number / patchset (not a synthetic ref); records that run's `run_id` on the batch for S8's confirmation.
- [ ] **FFO TOCTOU re-check:** immediately before the batch is handed off for submit, re-check the combined chain is still on the current `main` tip; if `main` advanced, re-assemble + re-batch — **bounded to `N=5` re-batch attempts**, after which the batch is dropped to the Phase-1 serial path (never hand off a stale tree, never loop unbounded). NOTE: the Phase-1 single-`wipChain` invariant does NOT hold in Phase 2 — this bounded re-batch loop is the mitigation.
- [ ] On green, **hand off to S8** (cast-Verified-per-member → ancestor-atomic submit) via the handoff record `{member_change_ids[], combined_tip_change_id, tested_sha, run_id}`. This story does **not** cast `Verified` and does **not** itself submit.
- [ ] Batch size bounded by a concrete numeric cap **`BATCH_MAX=8`** members per combined-tip CI run (sized to one run's job budget under the GHA concurrency cap); the cap is documented and enforced at assembly (excess changes wait for the next batch).

## Why
The DET floor is the ONLY blocking tier (every LLM criterion is advisory in v1). It must be a frozen,
deterministic, polyglot floor that fails open on any unsupported stack.

## What
- P1 readiness-shape; P2 file/symbol/import resolution (universal-ctags via the 8f6c oracle — LSP/solidlsp is the T2 follow-on `850f`, NOT v1); P3 package existence
  (deps.dev registry + optional syft SBOM); P4 oversize (scc/lizard metrics); P5 task-DAG validity + interference;
  P6 AC/DD quality; P7 destructive/irreversible sniff (escalates T4). The polyglot resolution/dependency/size tooling (P2/P3/P4) is CONSUMED — via the SHIPPED `refute_absence`/`applies`/`scan` facade — from the now-CLOSED prerequisite epic 8f6c-6008-33f3-4f82 (code-grounding oracle, `src/rebar/grounding/`) — this child does NOT re-build it; it owns the rebar-specific checks (P1/P5/P6/P7) + wiring P2/P3/P4 into the DET floor.

## Scope
- Call the 8f6c grounding-oracle facade (refute_absence/applies/scan); its three-valued abstain-by-default contract IS the fail-open guarantee — unsupported lang / no tool / parse-error / timeout -> abstain (recorded reason) -> skipped = PASS (ironclad).
- The shared oracle SHIPPED as prerequisite epic 8f6c (CLOSED; also consumed by code-review `9da1`); this child depends_on it and consumes it as a library, not as new integrations.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] P1-P7 implemented in Python, polyglot, fail-open (skipped=pass) tested per tool.
- [ ] Coverage recorded on the attestation.
- [ ] DET floor is the only tier that blocks BY DEFAULT in v1 (every LLM criterion is advisory; per-criterion LLM-tier blocking is OPT-IN via its `block_threshold` — 'DET-only' is the v1 default posture, not an architectural limit).

## (Added) P8 — reviewability / context-budget (DET)
A meta-finding, not tied to any one criterion, so it lives in the deterministic floor as P8: a DET check that
PASSES unless the ticket content (or a parent+child pairing for container criteria) EXCEEDS — or is
anticipated (token-estimate) to exceed — the largest configured context window even at one-criterion-per-call.
In that case it FAILS with 'ticket too big to review in full; reduce/decompose it' (the extreme of P4 oversize
/ G5 decomposition). Deterministic (a size/estimate check, no LLM); the orchestrator emits it during the
size-handling ladder.
## Acceptance Criteria (added)
- [ ] P8 reviewability DET check: passes unless content (or a parent+child pairing) exceeds — or is anticipated to exceed — the largest context window at one-criterion-per-call; else a 'ticket too big, reduce it' failure finding.

## Acceptance Criteria (added — T8 DET execution path)
- [ ] P1–P8 run as the deterministic `exec=DET` tier the orchestrator dispatches via its code executor (no LLM) — an explicit, first-class execution path, not merely a named tier.

## Context / Problem
RP-04 S7.3.a (`insincere-illogical-antlion`, 6633-219e-988a-42f6) records `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/binding_store.py` in its file impact because two legacy ambient config reads live there. RP-02 S2 (`brainy-cooked-hog`) MOVES both of them into the new `binding_lifecycle.py` owner, because they are lifecycle-policy config:

- `_env_int` — the defensive `os.environ.get` int parser (registry rationale cites `binding_store.py` L110; the line has already shifted once, to L109, from the RP-02 S1 T2 delegation)
- the `RECONCILER_ABSENT_RETIRE_GRACE` read that feeds the absence/retirement grace (registry rationale cites L538)

After the S2 move, S7.3.a's recorded target file no longer contains the reads it is meant to cut to the operation-snapshot seam.

## Why this needs its own ticket
The RP-02 <-> RP-04 coupling is deliberately recorded as a soft `relates_to` rather than a `depends_on`, so nothing enforces the retarget: RP-04 will silently miss the moved reads. This ticket is the durable artifact that prevents that.

`scripts/config_ownership_exceptions.py` keys `LEGACY_EXCEPTIONS` on PATH + SYMBOL (rows are `(relpath, symbol, rationale)`; line numbers appear only inside the human-readable rationale text). There are TWO entries for `binding_store.py` — one for `os.environ.get` and one for `RECONCILE R_ABSENT_RETIRE_GRACE` — so a path change makes both unregistered. RP-02 S2 re-registers them under `binding_lifecycle.py` in the same change so `make lint` stays green, but re-registering a moved legacy read is NOT resolving it: the read stays ambient, with byte-identical sourcing, defensive parse, default 3 and clamp minimum 1.
